newsitem.title: CHINA: China says opposed to European office in Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China says opposed to European office in Taiwan.

text.p: China said on Friday it was opposed to the European Parliament opening an office in rival Taiwan, urging the body not to harm bilateral ties.
"We are opposed to countries or organisations that have diplomatic relations with us engaging in contact with Taiwan of any official nature," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said in a statement.
"We...oppose the European Parliament establishing an office in Taiwan under any name," the spokesman said.

Taiwan's Foreign Minister John Chang, back in Taipei from a secrecy-cloaked visit to Europe and west Africa, said on Thursday the European Parliament had committed to opening a liaison office in Taipei.
European Parliament officials denied the move, but said the parliament had asked the European Union's executive Commission to set up an information office in Taipei.
Beijing and Taipei have been diplomatic rivals since the Communists won the Chinese civil war and drove the defeated Nationalists into exile on the island in 1949.
China regards Taiwan as a rebel province and has sought to push it into diplomatic isolation.
The spokesman urged the European Parliament "not to do anything that would harm bilateral relations". He declined to comment further.
